brief.title: Define a panel of independent reviewers
brief.plain_summary: From the plan or draft under review and the decision it informs, record who produced it and on which model family, pick three to five perspective cards, give each reviewer a family other than the producer's where one is available, and fix the shared packet, deadline and reading seed.
brief.outcome: A panel, with one give-view verb proposed per reviewer.

artifact.description: Pin of the plan, draft or proposal under review.

request.description: Pin of the requester's question: the decision the panel informs.

output_store.description: Store for the produced nouns. The default is a placeholder; use the store your owner assigned.

output_contract.delivery: Write produced nouns surface_only under your own authenticated surface, which is the requester's assigned surface, so the requester and that surface's reviewers can read them. Never use public_commons or allowlist other surfaces. Return every produced noun's pin in output.artifacts; add its value when the requester asks for inline delivery.

producer.on_panel is false and no reviewer is the producer.

No two reviewers share a perspective.

creates.nouns: The worker writes the nouns listed in output_contract.produces and returns their pins.
creates.verbs: The worker proposes follow-up verbs in output.proposed_verbs, such as a breakdown into smaller verbs or a research follow-up, with the pins they need. Proposals are never enqueued by the worker; an authorized requester enqueues the ones worth doing.

required: Verify the pins, and record who or what produced the artifact and its model family.
Pick perspective cards that differ, including one that looks for how the plan fails and one for the people it serves; write a new card in the same shape only when none fits.
Give each reviewer a family other than the producer's where the worker's allowance offers one, and name any same-family reviewer with the reason.
Fix the packet digest, a deadline and a reading seed, and propose one give-view verb per reviewer, each a separate attempt.
Return follow-up work the results justify as proposed_verbs and nouns worth creating later as proposed_nouns. Never enqueue them yourself; an authorized requester decides which to run.

brief.title: Give one independent view
brief.plain_summary: As one reviewer, read only the shared packet and your perspective card and give your own take: a stance, the points behind it with how sure you are of each, and what would change your mind.
brief.outcome: One reviewer's view, sealed on submission.

brief.title: Check the views' independence before anyone reads them
brief.plain_summary: Before any view is read for its content, confirm that each used the panel's packet, was sealed before the deadline and names no other reviewer, record each view's digest, exclude any whose independence is lost, and fix the reading order from the seed.
brief.outcome: An independence check that passes or says why not.

acceptance_checks.check: The check validates against template.independence-check's schema.
Every view_sha256 is the SHA-256 of that view's canonical JSON.
read_order is the included reviewer ids sorted by the SHA-256 of seed:reviewer_id.
result is passed only when same_packet and all_sealed_before_reading are true, no included view names another reviewer and at least three remain.

creates.nouns: The worker writes the nouns listed in output_contract.produces and returns their pins.
creates.verbs: The worker proposes follow-up verbs in output.proposed_verbs, such as a breakdown into smaller verbs or a research follow-up, with the pins they need. Proposals are never enqueued by the worker; an authorized requester enqueues the ones worth doing.

required: Verify the pins, and compute each view's SHA-256 over its canonical JSON.
Compare each view's packet digest with the panel's and each seal time with the deadline, marking late views.
Scan each view for other reviewers' ids and perspectives without weighing any view; exclude one that names or quotes another and propose a fresh give-view for that reviewer.
Order the reviewer ids by the SHA-256 of the seed, a colon and the id, and pass only when at least three independent views remain.
Return follow-up work the results justify as proposed_verbs and nouns worth creating later as proposed_nouns. Never enqueue them yourself; an authorized requester decides which to run.

brief.title: Synthesize where the reviewers disagree
brief.plain_summary: Read the sealed views in the fixed order and write a synthesis that leads with where reviewers disagree: each side quoted exactly with its reviewer and perspective, the kind of disagreement and where it goes next, then a short list of agreements and every point only one reviewer raised.
brief.outcome: A synthesis that decides nothing, with palette briefs for disagreements of taste.

acceptance_checks.check: The synthesis validates against template.synthesis's schema.
The synthesis passes every check in panel-checks.

required: Verify the pins; end blocked when the independence check did not pass, and confirm you neither produced the artifact nor wrote a view.
For each disagreement, quote every side exactly from its sealed view, name its kind and route, and say what would resolve it.

Propose the evaluation design pack's design-evaluation verb for a factual disagreement and write a palette brief for one of taste; a value disagreement goes to the person and one of scope to the requester.
List agreements briefly and every single-reviewer point; never turn a count of reviewers into a verdict, and run the panel checks before submitting.
Return follow-up work the results justify as proposed_verbs and nouns worth creating later as proposed_nouns. Never enqueue them yourself; an authorized requester decides which to run.
